correctness.rationale: Every legal new block contains the distinguished new point and an uncovered old pair. Two such blocks may not share an old vertex, because the pair formed by that old vertex and the new point would then occur twice. Thus k new blocks are in bijection with k-edge matchings of the leave, in both directions. The standard matching-polynomial substitution transfers Heilmann–Lieb real-rootedness to negative real zeros of the extension polynomial; Newton inequalities give the normalized ultra-log-concavity. The leave is a spanning subgraph of the complete graph, so edge addition only increases each matching count, and any old block removes leave edges already at degree one, proving the unique empty-system maximizer. An independent reconstruction reproduced the complete-graph coefficient rows through order seven exactly; the frozen verifier additionally exhausts all 5902 labelled PSTS through order seven and directly enumerates extensions through order five.

Those sources establish the underlying graph object and the relevance of matchings, but the inspected statements do not give the complete labelled one-new-point extension polynomial, its identification with the full matching generating polynomial, or the resulting real-rooted and ultra-log-concave extension strata. final_claim: For every finite partial Steiner triple system, the labelled induced one-point extension polynomial is exactly the matching generating polynomial of its leave; hence all zeros are negative real, the block-count strata are ultra-log-concave, and the empty partial triple system uniquely maximizes the total number of such extensions at fixed order.
